title: Hydrostatic bubbles of compressible fluid in an incompressible perfect fluid: the composition of the half-space operators
author: Juhi Jang, Ian Tice
work: Hydrostatic bubbles of compressible fluid in an incompressible perfect fluid
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem (source0.tex lines 1018--1027, source label hk_comp_Cm): the composition of the half-space operators associated with the compressible and incompressible problems equals the operator associated with the composed problem, in the sense of the stated identity between the two half-space Dirichlet-to-Neumann type operators; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 1028--1114 (one adjacent proof environment of 87 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span together with its retained context: it reduces the identity to the level of symbols, computes the symbol of each half-space operator from its definition, composes the two symbols and simplifies the resulting expression using the retained composition theorem and elementary algebra of the boundary symbols, and then transfers the symbolic identity back to the operators by the uniqueness of the operator with a given symbol on the half-space. This theorem is the operator-level step that allows the article to treat the two-fluid bubble problem as a single half-space problem. H2: a research-level partial-differential-equations theorem whose proof combines the calculus of half-space pseudodifferential symbols, composition of boundary operators and a uniqueness argument for operators with prescribed symbol; it is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
